subject: Hosted IO: standard per-1M token snapshot + model eligibility request
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira@tenantops.io>
To: alex.martinez@redwood.ai
Cc: elliot.ward@tenantops.io
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Quick ask: per-1M IO rates + supported model list (hosted)

Hi Alex,

We're evaluating hosted inference options for a pilot and I wanted to get a quick baseline from Redwood. Can you share the standard per-1M token rates (input vs output split) for hosted API, and a short list of supported model families (cost tiers) for generation + embedding workloads?

A few specifics:
- Pilot expected ~2.5M tokens/month to start, expected to ramp to ~25M over 6 months if metrics look good
- Need separate input and output rates for typical models (small/medium/large) and any difference for chat vs plain generation
- Are there quantized/low-cost variants you recommend if we care about unit economics?
- Any minimums, pilot credits, or standard discounts for committed volumes?

I've attached a short RFI spreadsheet with our targeted traffic and a couple of questions we didn't put in the body.

Thanks —
Samira
Head of ML Platform
TenantOps
[Attachment: TenantOps_RFI.xlsx (XLSX)]

From: alex.martinez@redwood.ai <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira@tenantops.io>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 11:00:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick ask: per-1M IO rates + supported model list (hosted)

Samira —

Thanks for the RFI and the context. Putting the short answers up front, and attaching our concise hosted ratecard for easy reference.

TL;DR (hosted API, per 1M tokens):
- Small gen (e.g., community-7B family): $3.50 per 1M tokens input / $7.00 per 1M tokens output
- Medium gen (e.g., mainstream 13B): $7.00 input / $14.00 output
- Large gen (70B+ family): $22.00 input / $44.00 output
- Embeddings (dense vector): $6.00 per 1M tokens (single unified rate)

Notes:
- Rates above are list (no commit). We offer tiered volume discounts (5-20%) for 3/6/12 month committed spend — we can show modeled cost curves based on your ramp assumptions.
- Quantized variants (x8/x4) are available for many gen families; quantized pricing typically reduces the gen rate by ~40–55% depending on throughput/latency SLO.
- Chat vs generation: same ratecard applies; we price by tokens in/out. For structured chat (tool-calling) there may be small additional per-call charges for tool payloads — we can map those in the pilot doc.

Attached: redwood-hosted-ratecard_v2.pdf — includes model family names, recommended quantization profiles, and a short guidance table for expected latency by hardware.

Next steps: happy to run a quick cost model against your RFI numbers. Are you available for a 30m call on Thursday (11/12) morning PT? If you'd like, I can loop in Rishi (our solutions engineer) to look at model selection and Monica for procurement/discount conversation.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132
[Attachment: redwood-hosted-ratecard_v2.pdf (PDF)]

Thanks Alex — quick follow-ups from our side after skimming the sheet:

1) For the pilot numbers, our expected token split is roughly 30% input / 70% output. Can you confirm how the example cost breaks down with that mix for the medium gen?
2) We care about burst capacity (we have daily spikes). Is burst included in hosted pricing or an add-on?
3) For embeddings: do you charge per 1M tokens processed to generate embeddings, or per 1M embedding requests? Our input is typically short texts (100–500 chars).
4) Any minimum commit level for discounts to apply? Our leadership prefers a single quarter commit to start (Q1).

Also — we prefer to evaluate quantized variants if latency is acceptable. Can Rishi or Monica share empirical latency/throughput numbers for the quantized 13B family?

Cheers,
Elliot
(also putting Samira on the loop)

Subject: Re: Quick ask: per-1M IO rates + supported model list (hosted)

Elliot/Samira —

Thanks for the questions — answers below, plus proposed next steps.

1) Example cost with 30/70 split (Medium gen list rates):
- Medium gen list: $7.00 per 1M input / $14.00 per 1M output
- Effective blended rate = (0.30 * $7.00) + (0.70 * $14.00) = $11.9 per 1M tokens
- On your pilot (2.5M tokens/mo) that maps to ~$29.75/mo list; at 25M tokens/mo it maps to ~$297.50/mo list.

2) Burst capacity: hosted includes a standard burst window for short spikes; for sustained high burst you can add a burst-reservation bump (one-time scaling knob) or move to a Dedicated pool. Burst-reservation pricing is a small percentage of monthly committed spend; we can include an exact line item in the pilot quote.

3) Embeddings billing: for short texts we bill per 1M tokens processed into the embedding model (not per embedding request). Typical tokenization for 100–500 chars is ~15–75 tokens, so your effective per-embedding cost will be low; we can map to your samples if you share 10 representative texts.

4) Discount minimums: our standard discounting tiers start at a 3-month commit for commercial discounts; single-quarter (Q1) commits are supported and typically qualify for the lower end of the discount range (5–8%); larger discounts require longer or larger commits. We can include an example term sheet for your procurement team.

Quantized latency/throughput: Rishi will send a short micro-benchmark doc in a separate email (13B x8 quantized median tail latency ~120–200ms for 32-token responses on our hosted fleet; throughput depends on concurrency and batching). Monica will follow up on commercial terms and standard pilot credit allowances (we typically offer $5k in credits for evaluation pilots over 30–60 days).

If this looks reasonable, propose we schedule a 30m call Friday 11/13 10:00am PT. On the call we can: walk your RFI numbers, select the right model family (gen vs quantized), and sketch a 90-day pilot scope + discount term.

Thanks —
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
